physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: After wound care, a patient asks the aide to post a photo of the incision on the clinic Instagram "to show how well they heal." What should the aide do?

options.a: Decline; clinic social posts of care photos need written authorization
options.b: Post after they agree out loud on the open gym floor
options.c: Crop the face but leave the chart sticker visible, then post
options.d: Post it, because an incision photo is not treated as PHI

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Photographs taken in care that can identify a patient are PHI. Marketing or social media use requires a valid written HIPAA authorization, not a hallway yes. Cropping a face while leaving a name sticker, or claiming a wound photo is not PHI, still discloses protected information.

distractorExplanations.b: Verbal agreement in a public gym is not a HIPAA authorization for marketing or social posts.
distractorExplanations.c: A chart sticker is an identifier; blurring a face does not de-identify the photo.
distractorExplanations.d: Images of a patient's body from treatment are PHI when they can be linked to that person.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: On a hallway walk the patient asks, "Am I getting better from the tear?" The aide has seen the evaluation. How should the aide answer?

options.a: Quote the MRI as a partial tear that heals in about six weeks
options.b: Drop the last two exercises because they look stronger today
options.c: Read a WebMD page that says walking every day will heal it
options.d: Say you cannot judge progress and have the PT talk with them

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Prognosis and interpretation of the evaluation belong to the licensed PT or PTA. An aide may encourage effort and report observations, but must not diagnose, quote imaging, change the program, or pull internet recovery timelines.

distractorExplanations.a: Explaining MRI findings and a recovery timeline is interpreting the evaluation, which is outside aide scope.
distractorExplanations.b: Dropping exercises is changing the plan of care, a licensed clinical decision.
distractorExplanations.c: Internet recovery claims are not the patient's plan and can give a false prognosis.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: A current outpatient the aide has been assisting texts after hours asking to meet for drinks this weekend. What is the correct action?

options.a: Accept the drinks if you meet well away from clinic property
options.b: Accept because the patient was the one who sent the first text
options.c: Decline and report the dual-relationship risk per clinic policy
options.d: Treat the invitation as private and never mention it at work

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: A romantic or social dating relationship with a current patient is a dual relationship and a boundary violation. Location and who initiated do not remove the power imbalance. Clinic policy usually requires declining and reporting so the case can be reassigned if needed.

distractorExplanations.a: Off-site dates still create a dual relationship with a current patient.
distractorExplanations.b: Staff own the boundary; patient-initiated contact does not make dating ethical.
distractorExplanations.d: Hiding the invitation prevents the clinic from managing the conflict and protecting the patient.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: A spouse waiting in the lobby asks the aide, "What did the PT say is wrong with their back?" What should the aide do?

options.a: Give a one-line diagnosis after they show the patient's ID card
options.b: Decline PHI in the lobby and send the spouse to speak with the PT
options.c: Share the diagnosis quietly because they are listed as next of kin
options.d: Text the diagnosis so people in the waiting room cannot overhear

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Diagnosis is PHI. Family status and an ID card do not, by themselves, authorize an aide to disclose it, and a lobby is not a private setting. Direct the spouse to the treating PT, who can confirm authorization and choose a private space if disclosure is allowed.

distractorExplanations.a: Showing an ID card does not prove the patient authorized this disclosure to the aide.
distractorExplanations.c: Next-of-kin status is not a blanket HIPAA authorization, and a lobby is public.
distractorExplanations.d: Texting PHI from an aide's phone is an unsecured disclosure the aide is not authorized to make.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: After a session the patient asks the aide to add three extra resistance-band sets "because the PT is too conservative." What should the aide do?

options.a: Keep the written plan and tell the PT about the extra-set request
options.b: Add the extra band sets if the patient signs a gym waiver first
options.c: Substitute a YouTube progression the patient already uses at home
options.d: Advance the band color today and chart the change as PT-approved

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Aides carry out the established plan of care; they do not progress load, add sets, or swap in outside programs. Capture the request and tell the PT or PTA, who may change the plan after a skilled decision.

distractorExplanations.b: A waiver does not authorize an aide to add volume beyond the written plan.
distractorExplanations.c: Home internet progressions are not the PT's plan and may be unsafe for this diagnosis.
distractorExplanations.d: Charting a self-made progression as PT-approved falsifies the record and exceeds scope.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: Mid-session the patient reports new numbness shooting into the foot that was not present at the start. The PT is in the next room. What should the aide do?

options.a: Finish remaining exercises, then mention it at the next scheduled visit
options.b: Keep going if the patient thinks the numbness is probably tightness
options.c: Stop the activity and notify the PT or PTA before you continue
options.d: Increase treadmill speed to test whether the numbness then clears

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: New neurologic symptoms are a change in status. Stop the task and report immediately to the PT or PTA so they can assess before anything else is done. Waiting until next visit, accepting the patient's self-diagnosis, or challenging the symptom with more intensity can worsen injury.

distractorExplanations.a: Delaying until the next visit withholds a status change the PT must know today.
distractorExplanations.b: The patient's guess of tightness does not replace licensed assessment of new numbness.
distractorExplanations.d: Speeding up to test numbness is an unlicensed clinical experiment and may worsen the finding.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: At discharge a grateful patient offers the aide a $200 cash envelope "just between us." Policy allows only small perishable tokens. What should the aide do?

options.a: Take the envelope because they insisted after you already said no
options.b: Split the cash with the desk so it is not a personal gift to you
options.c: Keep it because the episode of care is already closed on the chart
options.d: Decline the cash and report the offer under the clinic gift policy

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Large cash gifts create a dual relationship and a conflict of interest even at discharge. Follow clinic ethics: decline, do not split or hide it, and report so leadership can document the offer. Insistence and a closed episode do not override gift policy.

distractorExplanations.a: Repeated insistence does not convert a cash gift into an allowed token.
distractorExplanations.b: Sharing the cash still takes a prohibited gift; it remains a dual-relationship problem.
distractorExplanations.c: Discharge does not erase the recent treatment relationship or clinic gift rules.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: On the elevator with visitors aboard, a coworker starts venting about "the difficult ACL in room 3 who never does HEP." What should the aide do?

options.a: Stop them; identifiable case talk in a public elevator is a breach
options.b: Join in if nobody on the elevator uses the patient's legal full name
options.c: Keep venting because complaining about caseload is normal staff talk
options.d: Continue as long as you think only employees boarded at that floor

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Diagnosis, room number, and treatment details can identify a patient even without a name. Elevators are public. Stop the conversation and take any needed handoff to a private staff area. Staff-only intent does not make overheard PHI lawful.

distractorExplanations.b: Room, diagnosis, and HEP comments can identify someone without a legal name.
distractorExplanations.c: Venting about a case in public is still a privacy disclosure, not harmless shop talk.
distractorExplanations.d: Visitors may already be on the car; guessing who boarded does not protect PHI.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: The patient points at the printed evaluation and asks, "Does a 3+/5 on the quads mean I can stop using the brace?" What should the aide do?

options.a: Say 3+/5 means they can discontinue the brace starting this week
options.b: Recalculate the manual muscle grade from the printed eval numbers
options.c: Send that question to the PT; aides do not interpret eval findings
options.d: Say 3+/5 is a normal score, so the brace order was never required

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Manual muscle grades and brace decisions are skilled interpretation of the examination. Aides do not recast scores or discontinue equipment. Route the question to the PT, who wrote the eval and the brace order.

distractorExplanations.a: Linking an MMT grade to stopping a brace is interpreting the eval and changing the plan.
distractorExplanations.b: Recalculating MMT is performing examination scoring, which is not an aide duty.
distractorExplanations.d: Calling 3+/5 normal and voiding a brace order contradicts the PT's documented plan.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: During a transfer the aide's hand slips and the patient's knee hits the plinth. The patient laughs and says they are fine. What should the aide do?

options.a: Mention it to the PT on Friday if the knee still looks swollen
options.b: Skip reporting because the patient asked you not to make a fuss
options.c: Put a chart note only and skip filing the incident report form
options.d: Notify the PT now and complete the clinic incident report

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Any injury during care is reported immediately so the PT can examine the knee and the clinic can file the required incident record. Patient reassurance, delayed mention, or a chart note without the incident process can hide harm and block follow-up.

distractorExplanations.a: Waiting until Friday delays assessment of a possible acute injury.
distractorExplanations.b: A patient's request to avoid fuss does not cancel mandatory incident reporting.
distractorExplanations.c: A progress note does not replace the incident report required by clinic policy.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: The aide's close friend is added to today's schedule for gait practice, and the aide would be the only tech in the gym. What should the aide do?

options.a: Treat them anyway; a close friend is easier to guard and cue
options.b: Tell the PT about the dual relationship and ask to be reassigned
options.c: Treat them but leave the visit off the schedule for extra privacy
options.d: Offer a cash gait session after hours at the friend's apartment

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Providing therapy support to a close friend is a dual relationship that can bias guarding, documentation, and privacy. Disclose it to the PT and request reassignment. Hiding the visit or treating off-site after hours makes the conflict worse.

distractorExplanations.a: Friendship can bias safety decisions; it is a reason to recuse, not to treat.
distractorExplanations.c: Leaving a visit off the schedule falsifies the record and hides the dual relationship.
distractorExplanations.d: After-hours cash treatment of a friend is unlicensed practice plus a dual relationship.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: The aide leaves the front computer to grab linens. The screen still shows today's schedule with diagnoses, facing the waiting area. What should the aide do first?

options.a: Lock or log off before you leave so the lobby cannot read diagnoses
options.b: Leave the session open so the next aide can jump in without a login
options.c: Minimize the window, because diagnoses on a schedule are not PHI
options.d: Tilt the screen a little and assume visitors cannot read the names

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: A schedule that pairs names with diagnoses is PHI. Before walking away from a screen visible to the lobby, lock or log off. Leaving it open for convenience, minimizing it, or hoping the angle is enough are not reasonable safeguards.

distractorExplanations.b: An unlocked schedule facing visitors is a privacy incident waiting to happen.
distractorExplanations.c: Diagnoses tied to a named schedule are PHI even if the full chart is not open.
distractorExplanations.d: Screen angle is not a control; visitors can still read names and diagnoses.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: The written plan still lists 2-lb ankle weights. Yesterday those sets looked easy. The PT is in a meeting until the hour ends. What should the aide do on today's set?

options.a: Switch them to 5 lb because yesterday's 2 lb sets looked too easy
options.b: Drop the weights and start a new balance circuit from memory
options.c: Keep the 2 lb as written and tell the PT that it looked easy
options.d: Let the patient choose whichever ankle weight feels challenging

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Load progression is a skilled change to the plan of care. Until the PT or PTA updates the program, the aide keeps the documented 2 lb and reports that it looked easy. Patient-chosen load or a memory circuit is not a substitute for a licensed revision.

distractorExplanations.a: Jumping to 5 lb is progressing the plan without a PT or PTA decision.
distractorExplanations.b: Inventing a new circuit replaces the plan rather than following it.
distractorExplanations.d: Patient-selected load is not the established plan and can under- or overload the joint.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: A post-op patient asks the aide to skip the PT-ordered rest break and go straight to the next station so they can leave early for work. What should the aide do?

options.a: Skip the rest if they sign a note taking responsibility for leaving
options.b: Cut the rest in half as a compromise you think the PT would like
options.c: Rebuild the stations into a harder circuit so they can leave early
options.d: Keep the ordered rest and tell the PT about the request to skip

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Rest between stations can be part of the medical plan after surgery. An aide does not waive it for work schedules, half-cut it, or rebuild the circuit. Follow the ordered rest and report the request so the PT can decide whether timing can change.

distractorExplanations.a: A signed note does not transfer the PT's clinical responsibility to the patient.
distractorExplanations.b: Guessing a compromise still changes the ordered rest without a licensed decision.
distractorExplanations.c: A harder, shorter circuit is a new plan, not the one the PT wrote.

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.prompt: No PT or PTA is in the building at closing. The last patient asks the aide to "just run the ultrasound like last time." What should the aide do?

options.a: Run the unit while the PTA talks you through it on a cell phone
options.b: Decline; aides do not deliver ultrasound without required supervision
options.c: Run it at zero intensity and still bill the usual timed treatment
options.d: Have reception enter ultrasound as if the PT had just ordered it

physical-therapy-aide-readiness-check-et.explanation: Therapeutic ultrasound is a skilled modality. An aide must not apply it, especially with no supervising PT or PTA on site. Phone coaching, sham intensity with billing, and a desk-entered order are unlicensed practice and can be fraud.

distractorExplanations.a: Remote phone contact does not meet on-site supervision rules for an aide applying ultrasound.
distractorExplanations.c: Billing a sham treatment is fraud and still treats a modality the aide may not deliver.
distractorExplanations.d: Reception cannot create a skilled order; the aide would still be practicing without a license.
